newsitem.title: UK: Tanker rates mainly flat, modern ships favoured.
newsitem.headline: Tanker rates mainly flat, modern ships favoured.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates were flat on Friday with modern vessels having less trouble in getting fixed than older ships, brokers said.

Modern tonnage to Japan was able to achieve W68.5, as witnessed by the 1988-built 240,000 tonne Pacific Tower that was fixed at that level for Cosmo, while new ships on voyages west were done at W52.5/55.
But the picture was less rosy for older vessels, with the 1976-built Arcadian 1 fixed as low as W52.5 to the Philippines for Petron.
Brokers said the VLCC outlook for next week was uncertain.

"With Japanese charterers already having fixed cargoes as far ahead as 22 July, and Kuwaitis fixing off 28 July, owners of tonnage, particularly older units, might get a little nervous if there are no fresh cargoes forthcoming in the next few days," said Galbraith's Ltd in their weekly tanker report.
West Africa trade was thin with modern 130,000 tonne ships (Suezmaxes) to the U.S. achieving W87.5, and W85 to Europe.
Suezmaxes in the Med remained flat despite plenty of new business, with levels below W90 because of a surfeit of tonnage, especially older ships, brokers said.
Interest in 80,000 tonne (Aframax) vessels in the North Sea was patchy with rates weakening to W120 or below. Med Aframaxes suffered from an oversupply of tonnage and also dipped to around W115/120.
But Galbraith's said that "while North Sea rates are likely to slip further, it is probable that Mediterranean rates will creep up again in the next few days."

Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne vessels also dipped to W165 from W170/172.5, but remain well above the 1996 average of W148, according to data on Rigos Chartering Inc's Internet site. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
